overview: From 2026-09-20 to 2026-09-27, ethereum-optimism/optimism had 68 new PRs (41 merged), 22 new issues, and 60 active contributors.

topIssues.title: op-reth: eth_simulateV1 ignores the EIP-7825 gas cap on OP chains after reth v2.5.2
topIssues.author: sebastianst
topIssues.body:
Found while reviewing the reth v2.5.2 bump (#22495).

reth v2.5.2's `eth_simulateV1` sets `tx_gas_limit_cap = Some(u64::MAX)` whenever EIP-8037/Amsterdam is off ([`helpers/call.rs`](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/reth/blob/0fbe428518594611bdd3fdd822eb5968823c8e66/crates/rpc/rpc-eth-api/src/helpers/call.rs#L147-L151)), not only when `validation: false`. No OP fork maps to Amsterdam ([`spec.rs`](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/0f9780f366/rust/op-revm/src/spec.rs#L50)) and OP leaves the cap unset to use revm's spec-derived fallback ([`env.rs`](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/0f9780f366/rust/alloy-op-evm/src/env.rs#L123-L127)), so on every Karst+ chain a *validated* simulate accepts a transaction with `gas_limit > 2^24` that block validation rejects. `OpEthApi` inherits the default ([`call.rs`](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/0f9780f366/rust/op-reth/crates/rpc/src/eth/call.rs#L7)).

The upstream comment ties EIP-7825 to Amsterdam's accounting, but the cap itself is Osaka, so this looks wrong for L1 Osaka too. Options: upstream-first fix (lift the cap only when `validation` is false, or derive it from the spec), or an OP `simulate_v1` override. Either way `estimate_gas_7825`-style coverage exists for `eth_estimateGas` but not for simulate.

🤖 *Co-created with Claude Fable 5.1*

topIssues.title: rust: close the evidence gaps from the reth v2.5.2 / revm 42 / alloy 2.4 bump review
topIssues.author: sebastianst
topIssues.body:
Evidence gaps left open by the reth v2.5.2 / revm 42 / alloy 2.4 bump review (#22495). None is a known defect; each is a place where we rely on an upstream property without a local check.

1. **bn254 / BLS12-381 backend moved arkworks 0.5 → 0.6** (revm-precompile 42) for every build that does not enable revm's `bn` feature: op-reth, and cannon/asterisc kona-client ([`Cargo.toml`](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/0f9780f366/rust/kona/bin/client/Cargo.toml)); only the SP1 guest keeps the patched `substrate-bn` ([`Cargo.toml`](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/0f9780f366/rust/kona/sp1/programs/Cargo.toml#L127)). Curve constants are unchanged, but field and pairing code changed and this repo has no EIP-196/197/2537 vector tests; `revm-ee-tests` only asserts gas/halt shapes ([`op_revm_tests.rs`](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/0f9780f366/rust/revm-ee-tests/src/op_revm_tests.rs)). Add a small differential vector test (EEST vectors, arkworks vs substrate-bn); it also covers the pre-existing cannon-vs-SP1 backend split.
2. **c-kzg 2.1.7 → 2.1.8** with an `unsafe` transmute between alloy and `c_kzg::Blob` in kona's blob provider ([`blobs.rs`](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/0f9780f366/rust/kona/crates/providers/providers-alloy/src/blobs.rs#L111)); add a compile-time size/repr assertion.
3. **`AddressMap`/`B256Map` hasher** changed to `foldhash` in alloy-primitives 1.7 (iteration order now per-process random without the `rand` feature). Confirm no ordering dependence in the witness map ([`proof.rs`](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/0f9780f366/rust/op-reth/crates/trie/src/proof.rs#L367)) and `wiped_slots` ([`write.rs`](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/0f9780f366/rust/op-reth/crates/trie/src/db/store_v2/write.rs#L289)).
4. **`ExecutionPayloadFieldV2` deserialization**: alloy ≤ 2.1.1 matched V1 first and silently dropped `withdrawals` from a `getPayloadV2` response; 2.4.2 fixes it. kona's seal task consumes it ([`task.rs`](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/0f9780f366/rust/kona/crates/node/engine/src/task_queue/tasks/seal/task.rs#L129)); add a regression test so the fix does not rest on the pin alone.
5. **Receipt/log/block decode strictness**: alloy 2.4 rejects non-canonical `Eip658Value` bytes, string-wrapped logs and trailing bytes in sealed blocks, closing Go↔Rust leniency gaps on oracle-supplied receipts ([`provider.rs`](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/0f9780f366/rust/kona/crates/proof/proof-interop/src/provider.rs#L125)). Pin with outcome-based op-alloy tests.
6. **Trace replay by index**: reth now stops block replay at the transaction *index*; op-reth's `transaction_by_hash` override supplies that index from a flashblock ([`transaction.rs`](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/0f9780f366/rust/op-reth/crates/rpc/src/eth/transaction.rs#L243-L255)). Add a test tracing a transaction present in both the pending flashblock and the sealed block.
7. **SSTORE cold-load skip threshold** moved 2000 → 2100 (revm 42, Berlin-gated): gas outcome unchanged, but a slot the old code read before OOG is no longer read, so `debug_executionWitness` content can differ between revm-41 and revm-42 nodes. Roll op-reth together with the matching kona prestate.

🤖 *Co-created with Claude Fable 5.1*

topIssues.title: op-reth: pin OP engine defaults and audit deployments for reth v2.5.2 flag changes
topIssues.author: sebastianst
topIssues.body:
Found while reviewing the reth v2.5.2 bump (#22495). Operator-facing changes inherited from upstream; op-reth sets no engine defaults of its own.

**Defaults moved** (visible in the CLI snapshot, [`cli.snap`](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/0f9780f366/rust/op-reth/crates/cli/tests/snapshots/cli.snap#L250-L252)): `--engine.persistence-threshold` 2 → 7; `--engine.memory-block-buffer-target` default 0 → `min(threshold, 5)`; `--engine.persistence-backpressure-threshold` (still 16) is now measured *beyond* the buffer target, so the stall point moves from 16 to ~21 unpersisted blocks. On 2 s or sub-second OP block times the DB tip lags the head by 5 blocks and up to 7 may be unpersisted: larger crash-recovery redo window and engine memory.

**Startup constraints** (`EngineArgs::validate`): buffer target must not exceed the threshold; masking blocks + buffer must stay below the threshold; `--engine.txpool-prewarming` conflicts with `--engine.disable-state-cache`. A deployment passing e.g. `--engine.memory-block-buffer-target 5 --engine.persistence-threshold 2` now fails to start. `--engine.sparse-trie-max-hot-slots` / `-storage-tries` / `-accounts` were removed (clap rejects them) and the `sparse_trie_retained_memory_bytes` gauge is gone.

**Env-activated flags**: `--engine.txpool-prewarming` and `--engine.sender-recovery-cache` read `RETH_ENGINE_TXPOOL_PREWARMING` / `RETH_ENGINE_SENDER_RECOVERY_CACHE`. The recovery cache is populated by the network component on OP but never read: `OpEvmConfig` recovers senders directly ([`lib.rs`](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/0f9780f366/rust/op-reth/crates/evm/src/lib.rs#L325-L331)), unlike `EthEvmConfig`.

**Other**: `reth.toml` `bootnodes` now takes precedence over the superchain-registry bootnodes; RocksDB keeps all files open when `RLIMIT_NOFILE >= 128k`.

Proposed: (1) pin OP-specific engine defaults with `DefaultEngineValues::try_init` ([`engine.rs`](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/reth/blob/0fbe428518594611bdd3fdd822eb5968823c8e66/crates/node/core/src/args/engine.rs#L63)) so upstream tuning churn shows up in our diff instead of silently; (2) audit deployed engine flags (k8s, devnets) before rolling out; (3) either wire `SenderRecoveryCache` into `OpEvmConfig` or make the flag a no-op on OP.

🤖 *Co-created with Claude Fable 5.1*

topIssues.title: op-revm: make the deposit gas-cap exemption a property of OpHandler::tx_gas
topIssues.author: sebastianst
topIssues.body:
Found while reviewing the reth v2.5.2 bump (#22495).

Deposits are exempt from the EIP-7825 transaction gas cap. Today that exemption is implemented only in `alloy_op_evm::OpEvm::transact_raw`, which temporarily replaces `cfg.tx_gas_limit_cap` with `u64::MAX` around a deposit ([`lib.rs`](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/0f9780f366/rust/alloy-op-evm/src/lib.rs#L363-L376)). `OpHandler` itself does not override the gas split: revm 42 moved `initial_gas_and_reservoir` into a new defaulted `Handler::tx_gas` (`revm-handler` 42.0.1, `handler.rs:215`), called from `run_without_catch_error`, `run_system_call`, `runtime_oog_result` and the inspector path. A consumer driving published `op-revm` directly (`ExecuteEvm::transact`/`replay`/`transact_commit`) therefore hands an oversized deposit `cap - intrinsic` regular gas and parks the rest in the EIP-8037 reservoir, i.e. a spuriously OOG deposit. `op-revm` is a published crate; Flashbots' `op-rbuilder` redirects it to this repo via `[patch.crates-io]`.

Proposed: override `Handler::tx_gas` in `OpHandler` to pass `u64::MAX` for `DEPOSIT_TRANSACTION_TYPE` (next to the existing deposit skip in `validate_env`, [`handler.rs`](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/0f9780f366/rust/op-revm/src/handler.rs#L89)), then delete the save/restore in alloy-op-evm. The two deposit-cap tests in `alloy-op-evm/src/tests.rs` should keep passing unchanged, plus a new op-revm-level test.

🤖 *Co-created with Claude Fable 5.1*

topPRs.title: op-private-interop!: establish the private-chain PoC reference
topPRs.author: karlfloersch
topPRs.body:
Establishes an upstream draft reference for the private-chain interop PoC, including private execution, deterministic public projection, message-position resolution before publication, and persistent LightCL recovery. This is experimental work intended for eventual upstreaming after substantial review and refinement.

Projection spans are admitted as a whole before derivation releases their first new block. A pure Go/Kona validator enforces the transaction grammar, claim framing, per-block private OutputV0 records, and the span proof statement. After invalidation or sequencing-window expiry, publication binds to the canonical public parent and the last surviving private checkpoint, including a commitment to intervening replacement inputs. LightCL checks the local private output against the surviving record before adopting it, then retains its rewind, deposit-only replacement, and restart safeguards.

The verifier remains an explicitly configured insecure stub: publication is operator-attested, and private execution correspondence is not cryptographically verified. Protocol fallback blocks need no publisher proof; a future real proof must cover private execution through their recovery interval. This profile requires fresh deployments with interop and Isthmus active at genesis. Published spans cannot cross future activation blocks under the current rules. Initiating messages retain upstream's strict earlier-timestamp rule; same-timestamp dependencies remain unsupported. Private execution proofs, complete fault-proof execution support, and native ETH bridging/withdrawal settlement remain outside the supported profile.

Validation: targeted Go suites and repository Go lint pass; 662 affected Rust tests, strict clippy, no-std, feature propagation and SP1 guest lock checks pass; 31 private-profile Solidity tests plus three cross-language claim-vector tests pass. A fresh op-up private-interop smoke run passes. The full devstack/sysgo private-interop acceptance run passes all 13 enabled tests in 37m23s, including outage/expiry, invalidation, L1 reorgs, interrupted recovery, and restart after newer valid history. Changed registry artifacts and its interface pass scoped verification. Repository-wide contract tooling also encounters unchanged dispute-game interface mismatches and conflicting duplicate ZK-game build artifacts; those unrelated files are outside this update. The optional production-cadence soaks have not been repeated for this change. Two independent scoped reviews covered derivation parity, recovery, and public-source publication; broader production/security and full-feature reviews remain necessary.

Known existing CI issue: broad acceptance shards previously exposed the ordinary-follow finality guard rejecting stock EL-sync bootstrap snapshots whose follower finalized label is ahead of its source. That guard is unchanged by this update and remains an open issue for the recovery stack. Prior CI results do not establish that this revision is green.

This reference excludes atomic coordinator/shared-block builder work and local deployment artifacts. It does not update running devnet images.

**BREAKING CHANGE:** the new claim wire format, per-block output records, contract bytecode and private genesis-output configuration require matching clients/contracts and fresh databases. Preserve the private recovery journal alongside the private execution database. Unsupported private native bridge routes must remain disabled.

topPRs.title: op-private-interop,contracts!: derive and recover a private ETH chain public projection
topPRs.author: karlfloersch
topPRs.body:
Private interop keeps application execution private while publishing the message history needed by the public interop set. One private-chain genesis produces a deterministic public projection, using standard span-batch transport and cross-chain dependency checks. This replaces #22729 and uses the existing `private-interop/devnet-readiness` branch unchanged at `9f679db23ac12be10049766843495a03eb2993c2`.

Ordinary L1 deposits execute against private state. On the public projection, user deposits are included as successful no-ops with no minting, state changes, execution gas or logs; authenticated system deposits still execute. After sequencing-window expiry, interop invalidation or an L1 reorg, the private node returns to a surviving authenticated checkpoint and rebuilds canonical deposit-only intervals before publication resumes. Recovery ancestry persists across restarts, and batch publication waits for private reconciliation and an authorized batcher epoch.

The PoC remains operator-attested; execution-proof enforcement and private withdrawal settlement are future work. Native ETH bridge routes remain disabled in the private profile. The diff also includes the companion L1 event-certificate contracts, which are separate from the projection mechanism. Versioned bundle tooling, remote private-pair smoke, and deposit/recovery/reorg/rotation/cadence tests support devnet preparation.

**BREAKING CHANGE:** projection deposit execution, the claimed-follow RPC and recovery journal configuration require matching clients/contracts and fresh databases when migrating from earlier prototypes. Configure the persistent recovery path and ordinary projection rollup RPC as documented in [DEVNET.md](https://github.com/karlfloersch/optimism/blob/9f679db23ac12be10049766843495a03eb2993c2/op-private-interop/docs/DEVNET.md). Installing the custom native ETH bridge implementation requires explicit send/relay permissions.

Validation on this unchanged revision:

- Fourteen targeted Go test packages pass, covering private interop, batcher, claim-follow, chain container, driver, engine, sequencing, source client, smoke and devstack.
- Ten focused Rust projection/genesis tests and 78 targeted Solidity tests pass (Foundry lite profile). Main-workspace and SP1-guest Rust formatting pass.
- Full Go lint finds two existing issues: unchecked `big.Int.Uint64` in the position resolver and import ordering in the private interop preset. The fixes prepared locally are intentionally excluded to preserve this revision.
- Current upstream `develop` has three merge conflicts with this branch, in devstack configuration/signer setup. No upstream reconciliation is included.
- Full protocol/security review, full devnet acceptance and the production-cadence soak remain outstanding for this draft.

topPRs.title: feat: add private interop cleanroom implementation
topPRs.author: opsuperchain
topPRs.body:
## Summary

- add the private-interop private/rendering chain pair, contracts, deterministic rendering codec, builder, and claim-follow path
- integrate the pair with op-deployer, op-batcher, op-supernode, op-interop-filter, devstack, and op-up
- add private-pair-aware interop smoke coverage and a design document
- harden the implementation after adversarial review: structurally close deposits, bind rendering inputs and emitters, cap amplification, remove the separate operator key/premine, disable the stock ETH path, and make rendering execution fully zero-fee

## `op-up --private-interop` topology

```text
                         L1 EL + beacon node
                          ^              |
                          | batches      | derives
         +----------------+---+      +---v-----------------+
         |                    |      |                     |
   normal A batcher    private-interop batcher       shared supernode
         ^                    ^                      public view: {A, B-render}
         |                    |                         |          |
 A sequencer op-node   B private op-node               |          |
         |                    |                         |          |
 A sequencer op-reth   B private op-reth         A verifier   B rendering
   public chain 901    private chain 902           op-reth       op-reth
                              ^                                     |
                              +------ `/902/claimed` ----------------+
```

- Chain A is an ordinary public OP chain with a stock batcher and proposer.
- Chain B has two different histories sharing chain ID 902: the sequenced, user-facing custom-gas-token private chain and a public, derived-only rendering with no sequencer or mempool.
- The private-interop batcher reads private B blocks, converts exported logs into claim/replay transactions, checks the rendering parent, and posts an ordinary channel to L1.
- The shared supernode derives and judges `{A, B-render}` using the stock message database and cross-safety logic. It has no private-chain access and does not know that B is a rendering.
- The only private-interop addition in the supernode is the `/902/claimed` follow endpoint. It reconstructs the committed private-B safe block reference from public rendering claims for the private op-node; it does not alter judging.
- Private B and rendering B are never P2P-peered: they deliberately have the same chain ID but different genesis hashes and block contents.
- `--smoke` runs `interopsmoke` in the same process so private receipt positions can be resolved to their canonical public rendering positions.

## Verification

- `go test ./op-batcher/batcher ./op-chain-ops/interopsmoke/... ./op-deployer/pkg/deployer/state ./op-interop-filter/filter ./op-private-interop/... ./op-supernode/supernode/chain_container -count=1`
- focused op-deployer private-interop genesis/rollup integration tests
- 49/49 private-interop Solidity tests
- 24/24 L2-to-L2 messenger Solidity tests
- 15/15 L2 genesis Solidity tests
- `op-up --private-interop --smoke`: chain identity, native transfers, valid messages in both directions, rendered private-chain message resolution, and invalid-message reorg all pass

## Notes

This is intentionally a draft for design and security review. The stock Superchain ETH bridge smoke case is skipped on the custom-gas-token private half; that path is closed by design and `NativeMintBridge` is the sanctioned liquidity path.

topPRs.title: kona-node,kona-chainview: pilot a SQL chain view compiled by Feldera behind the chainview feature
topPRs.author: teddyknox
topPRs.body:
**Experiment, not a merge proposal.** This is the pilot from a design study on using upstream Feldera (crates.io `dbsp` + the `sql-to-dbsp` compiler, no fork) to replace hand-maintained derived state in kona-node with one incrementally maintained circuit. It is opened as a draft so the delta can be discussed with real code and numbers; the write-up with the reasoning, the reflections, and the proposed next steps is the design study `docs/feldera-in-kona-node.md` in the opql repo (rendered copy: https://claude.ai/code/artifact/a3ea095f-5297-4c98-8841-35f6008f0fe7).

**Why.** kona-node keeps the consequences of chain facts in several places by hand: the safe head is copied into four structures, one L1 poll fans out to three consumers, finality lives in a map that is cleared on every pipeline reset and finalizes by number, `optimism_syncStatus` makes three L1 RPCs per call, and `optimism_safeHeadAtL1Block` is unimplemented. Each copy is a place for a reorg or a reset to leave state behind.

**What changes for an operator.** The chain view is not optional: the paths it replaces are deleted, not gated. Concretely:

- Finality is driven by the chain view's `finalized_l2` view and sent to the engine by hash, guarded to be above the engine's finalized head and at or below the last confirmed safe head. It survives pipeline resets. `L2Finalizer`, the finalized-L1 fan-out to derivation, and finalize-by-number are gone.
- `optimism_syncStatus` serves its L1 fields from the chain view's snapshot with no L1 RPC on the request path; the watcher's three-RPC `L1State` query is gone.
- `optimism_safeHeadAtL1Block` is implemented with op-node's SafeDB semantics (nearest entry at or below the requested L1 block; not persisted across restarts).
- The gossip signer is read from the `SystemConfig` contract at every polled L1 head (one storage read per head) instead of scanned from that head's logs, so a rotation in a skipped block is no longer lost; the watcher's per-chain signer scan is gone.
- The chain view's L1 blocks are the derivation pipeline's own traversal: the derivation actor pushes every origin it advances through, including the heights it re-walks after a reset. There is no separate L1 walk, no window, no backfill at startup, no flag, and no L1 read beyond the signer's. The L1 watcher only polls the head, safe and finalized tags, publishes them on watch channels, and fans heads out to derivation.
- The engine's imported blocks are held by the chain view (the newest 256 at or above the engine's finalized head, pruned as finality advances) and served to derivation's hash-keyed block and `SystemConfig` lookups through a small `ImportedL2Blocks` trait in `kona-providers-alloy`, so that crate and the host binary that depends on it stay free of the chain view. `kona-providers-local`, a 32-block LRU with chain-event and reorg-depth handling that nothing in the node fed, is deleted.

**Size.** Against `develop`, lockfile excluded: the new crate is 2,124 lines (1,754 product including `build.rs` and its README, 370 tests). kona's existing crates gain 752 product and 339 test lines and lose 2,286: the finalizer, the finalized-L1 fan-out, the signer scan, the `L1State` query, `kona-providers-local`, and their tests.

**Reasons a reviewer cannot see in the diff.**

- The SQL program (`crates/node/chainview/src/chainview.sql`) is compiled at build time by Feldera's `sql-to-dbsp` v0.342.0, shipped as a sha256-pinned release JAR that `build.rs` locates but never downloads (`just chainview-fetch-compiler` fetches and verifies it). This adds JDK 21 and the JAR as prerequisites for every `--workspace` / `--all-features` build, so **the Rust CI jobs are expected to fail on this PR** until either the CI image carries both or the crate leaves the default workspace members. That is one of the open questions, not an oversight.
- Every table is a plain Z-set with no primary key: a reorg is a retraction and a status change is a retract-and-insert, so the circuit is never reset. The only command a view drives is the monotone finalize; nothing else asserts what was done.
- The held L2 blocks are host state in the driver, not a table: no view needs a block body, and the driver already tracks the finalized head that prunes them. A SystemConfig fold was built and then removed because nothing consumed it; derivation keeps its own.
- `Engine::reset` now publishes the post-reset state on its watch channel (one line, unconditional). Without it the chain view saw pre-reset heads until the next task.
- The multi-chain watcher keeps its per-chain derivation fan-out and config queries. The view's L1 facts come from each chain's derivation actor, so a multi-chain host would get them per chain; the L1 tag statuses and the signer read are per node for now.
- Reorgs need no code of their own in the view: the pipeline re-walks the heights it rewound over after a reset, and an origin that arrives at a height already held with another hash replaces it and its update rows.

**Validation.** Circuit-level tests through the typed handles (finality, safe-head guard, L1 reorg replacement, reset retraction, nearest-at-or-below lookup, signer rotation and rollback, finalized pruning, the held blocks' cap and pruning, LATENESS drops); host tests for the derivation actor's origin publishing, finalize guard and confirmation pairing, the chain-view actor's tag statuses and signer read, the watcher's fan-out and watches, and the providers wrapper's local-first lookups; clippy `-D warnings` and rustfmt clean. sysgo: a new `TestSafeHeadHistoryMatchesOpNodeSafeDB` compares kona's `safeHeadAtL1Block` history against op-node's SafeDB on a mixed devnet with the DSL's own comparison; it passes on `develop` (24 safe blocks across several L1 blocks, every entry equal), as do the full `node/common` package (one pre-existing skip) and `node/restart`, and all three suites were re-run after each cut, the last one included. `node/reorgs` was not rerun on `develop`; on the original base its one failing subtest failed with the feature off as well. Both nodes' `syncStatus` L1 fields agreed throughout. Not run: a soak, an induced L1 reorg, and a signer rotation on a devnet.

**Found in passing.** Two things worth knowing beyond this PR:

- kona-node enables its Prometheus listener on port 9090 with no metrics flags set, so two kona-nodes on one host collide at startup ("Address already in use"); the parallel sysgo suites need `KONA_METRICS_ENABLED=false`. Not fixed here.
- The global `--metrics.enabled` has clap id `enabled` (its field name), and clap propagates a global argument's explicit value into every subcommand under that id. Any `node` subcommand flag whose field is also named `enabled` is silently overwritten, which is how `KONA_METRICS_ENABLED=false` switched an earlier, optional version of the chain view off during validation. There is no such flag any more, but the trap is live for any future `enabled` field on a subcommand.

**Reviews.** The repo's `rust-code-reviewer` and `go-code-reviewer` guides were applied as two independent review passes before opening. Fixed from them: the finality guard compared numbers only (now also the hash at the safe height, and a reset retracts an equal-height row with another hash); the safe-head history was unbounded (now capped, default 8192 entries); `LATENESS` was unchecked against the chain's `seq_window_size + channel_timeout` (the node now refuses to start when it would drop re-derived rows); the sysgo test hand-rolled the SafeDB walk (now the DSL's `VerifySafeHeadDatabaseMatches`); dead API and unused dependencies. Their findings on the separate canonical L1 walk (re-anchor seed rows, failing closed below the window, retrying transient reads) were fixed and then made moot by removing the walk in favour of the pipeline's traversal; the SystemConfig fold and its per-block log read went with it. Dismissed or deferred: a unit test for the one-line `Engine::reset` publish (no mock engine client exists; it is its own commit instead), hoisting the signer storage-slot read shared with `flags/p2p.rs` (touches unrelated CLI code), and the CI/Java question above, which is the PR's main open point.

topPRs.title: op-e2e/actions: run the action tests on the out-of-process op-reth-test-engine
topPRs.author: sebastianst
topPRs.body:
Switches `op-e2e/actions` to run against the out-of-process `op-reth-test-engine` (stacked on #21242), selected by `OP_E2E_ACTIONS_EL=reth-test-engine`. The default stays op-geth, and CI now runs the whole actions suite on **both** ELs.

## Gate: same pass-set on both ELs

Full sweep over all 13 `op-e2e/actions` packages at this head: **identical per-test results on both ELs** (225+ tests) — including the reorg suite (ReorgFlipFlop, DeepReorg, rewind, Holocene invalid-payload replacement), EL-sync (all 5 sync tests via the in-process sync-pump emulation), batcher garbage/blob paths, sequencer drift, altda challenge/expire, supernode rewind, and the engine-API tests. The only intended divergence:

- `RestartOpGeth` (op-geth persistent-DataDir restart-recovery) is geth-gated — impossible against an ephemeral subprocess. Its durable behavior is covered on **both** ELs by the new `RestartEngineFreshState`: restart the engine with all state lost; op-node resets against the wiped engine, re-derives the safe chain from L1 (safety + finality restored), and the sequencer re-builds the identical deposit-only unsafe chain. The geth-only test is deleted in the stacked deletion PR.
- One rare pre-existing-style flake was investigated and ruled out as a divergence: `FinalizeWhileSyncing` failed once in ~45+ runs, does not touch any of the new wiring (no peering/pump), and did not reproduce in 25 dedicated runs on the pre-wiring base.

## Go-side switch (mechanical rewrites, each enumerable)

- ~100 `engine.L2Chain()` sites → backend-agnostic helpers (`LatestHeader`/`SafeHeader`/`FinalizedHeader`/`BlockByNumber` over the eth RPC).
- `ActL2IncludeTx` reframed onto the engine's parking buffer (`optest_includeNextTx`); `RemainingBlockGas`/`ForcedEmpty` via `optest_*`; blob-tx rejection asserts each EL's own irreducible message.
- EL-sync p2p emulation: a package registry maps synthetic enode IDs to reth backends; `AddPeers` starts a per-peer sync pump that backfills `optest_syncTarget`-signalled gaps via `optest_blockPayloadByNumber`→`optest_importBlock`, never moving safe/finalized — reproducing op-geth's post-snap-sync state and log lines.

## Engine additions the switch forced (same crate as #21242)

- **Reorg support**: `new_payload` records every validated block; forkchoice update canonicalizes via `NewCanonicalChain::Reorg` (the engine-tree pattern), so alternate forks, flip-flops, and rewinds work. Invalid payload attributes surface as `-38003` so op-node falls back to deposits-only blocks.
- **Engine-API-faithful canonicalization**: processed payloads stay non-canonical until FCU (the geth engine test asserts exactly this gap).
- Richer reads (`eth_call`/`estimateGas`, OP-enriched receipts, historical `eth_getProof`) plus differential tests proving op-node decodes/validates reth receipts-roots and proofs, and that `eth_estimateGas` matches op-geth byte-for-byte on the action-test genesis.

## CI

`go-actions-tests-reth` runs `./op-e2e/actions/...` on the reth engine (binary from `rust-workspace-binaries`, `REQUIRE_RUST_ENGINE=1` + hard binary check so provisioning bugs fail loudly), wired into `ci-gate`. The geth side keeps running in `go-tests-short`/`go-tests-full`, so this PR puts the A/B comparison permanently in CI.

Part of #21196 (Go side) and #20415 (engine design).
